summary: Otto Rosenberg (1888–1919) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1906–1910) under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and Sergey Oldenburg, the University of Bonn (1909), and under Rudolf Lange (~1911–1912), later teaching at Saint Petersburg.

Otto Stein (1893–1942) was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at Charles University (1912–1918) under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda. He joined the Oriental Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences in 1929 and succeeded Winternitz.

Otto Strauss (1881–1940) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel (under Hermann Oldenberg and Paul Deussen). He held professorships at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), Kiel (1920), and Breslau (1928–1935).

Otto von Böhtlingk (1815–1904) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn (under Christian Lassen and Franz Bopp). He served at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (~1842–1904, director 1849–1868) and the University of Jena (~1868–1885).

Owen Flanagan (1949–) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fordham University (~1966–1970) and Boston University (~1972–1977), and became Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri (1890–1978) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bishop Heber College, Saidapet, and the University of Madras. He served as professor at Bishop Heber College, principal of Rajah's College, and department head at Annamalai University.
P. T. Narasimhachar (1905–1998) was an Indologist. He completed his studies at Maharaja's College, Mysore, between ~1923 and 1927 under Mysore Hiriyanna.

Padma Subrahmanyam (1943–) is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Ethiraj College for Women, Stella Maris College, and Annamalai University, conducting research under the supervision of T. N. Ramachandran.

Padmanabh S. Jaini (1923–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, attested from 1977 to 1990 and in 2002, later becoming professor emeritus.

Pahalawattage Don Premasiri (1941–) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi, he studied under David J. Kalupahana and Eliot Deutsch, later serving as professor and Pali and Buddhist Studies Department head at the University of Peradeniya.

Palmira Brummett (1950–) is a historian and archaeologist. She studied at the University of Chicago (B.A., 1975) and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (M.P.H., 1981), later holding posts at the University of Tennessee (~1990–2011) and Brown University (2011–2016).
Palmo Kyi is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She studied under teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal, and was supervised by Per Kværne (attested 2012).

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She held an affiliation at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She pursued her studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University (~1971–1976).

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indologist and historian educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He served as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949) and National Professor of Indology for the Government of India (~1959–1972).
Parashuram Krishna Gode (1891–1961) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Curator at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1916 to 1946 and ~1919 to 1961.

Parimal G. Patil works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at Harvard University (~1993–1997) and the University of Chicago (~1997–2002), and became a Professor at Harvard University around 2004.

Parul Dave-Mukherji specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford (1988–1991) under Alexis Sanderson and is attested as professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2020.

Pasang Wangdu (1952–2024) was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Supervised by Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner, he served as a professor at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, attested from 2006 to 2014.

Pascale Haag (1965–) works in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat and Marie-Claire Gay at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1996–2002) and Paris Nanterre University (~2013–2018), and held a post at the EHESS around 2004.
